# gpueuro #3: Verda raises prices 3 times in a week

Gunars Mie

Oct 26, 2026

Prices checked 26 Oct 2026. On-demand, per GPU-hour, ex-VAT.

Verda raised its on-demand prices 3 times in one week. Our daily checks of Verda’s EUR price page found steps on 21, 24 and 25 Oct. The H100 went from €3.82 to €4.07 (+6.5%). That makes Verda’s H100 the most expensive of the six we rank, at more than double Seeweb’s €1.89.

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

GPUJournal reads providers' own published pricing pages and banks the figures at every check. The checks behind this page fell on Oct 19, 22, 23, 24 and 26, 2026 — there are gaps between them, so the October rises are documented check by check rather than day by day. A price change we catch in our own checks is only reported when both the before and after figures were seen on the provider's own page, each with its date; that is how the Verda and RunPod rises above were verified. The Nebius rise of Oct 1, 2026 is different: it predates our records and was an announced rise, so we did not bank both sides of it ourselves — we verified the post-rise rates on Nebius's own page (checked Oct 19, re-read unchanged Oct 26) and report it as announced. And a price a provider merely states about itself never appears on our board as a verified price. Where a provider's pages state figures we cannot verify, Price Watch reports them labelled as stated — which is how disagreements get exposed rather than hidden: on Oct 26, Spheron's pages stated the same H100 at $2.64 on some pages and $2.98 on others, and we report the disagreement rather than pick a number.

Verda, the former DataCrunch, lists a 1x B200 SXM6 180GB instance at $7.87 an hour on demand, up from $6.85 in our September survey, and $3.94 on spot, with 30 CPUs and 170 GB of RAM per GPU 7. It also sells the B200 as serverless containers at $8.66, or $4.33 on spot, and as instant clusters at $7.87 per GPU. Long-term discounts on self-service instances run from 2 percent for one month to 8 percent for a year and 25 percent for two years, which puts a two-year B200 at about $5.90 per GPU-hour. Verda's spot tier is one of the few fixed B200 spot prices below $4 that were actually in stock, according to GetDeploying, which makes it the main alternative to GPUBank's $2.49 interruptible hour for European workloads that can live with interruption 15. 7

results.title: Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead
results.author: Lindstead
highlights:
Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs.

On-demand price of one H100 per hour, September to October:
• Nebius (NL): €3.38 to €3.95, up 17%
• Scaleway (FR): €2.73 to €2.87, up 5%
• Verda (FI): €3.09 to €3.18, up 3%

Nebius raised its newest GPUs most. A B300 now costs €8.33 an hour, up 21 percent. OVHcloud and Hetzner did not change their prices.

results.title: Where to rent an A100 SXM at the cheapest price - GPUBank
results.author: GPUBank Research
highlights: Beyond the six offers shown as cards, several managed clouds sell a single A100 80 GB at prices between $1.36 and $2.00. Beam lists an A100 80 GB SXM4 machine from $1.36 an hour with 16 vCPU, 128 GB of RAM and 1 TB of NVMe, one of the most generous machines in this price range 16. Jarvislabs charges $1.49 with 16 vCPU and 112 GB of RAM, billed per minute, without saying SXM or PCIe on its pricing page, and GetDeploying showed Geodd's A100 SXM with 16 vCPU and 120 GB and Sesterce's unlabelled A100 80 GB, both at $1.49 and in stock on 15 October 9; and Hyperstack lists its A100 SXM at $1.60 on demand and $1.36 reserved, with up to 24 pCPU and 120 GB of RAM, next to a PCIe A100 at $1.35 12 18. Verda, formerly DataCrunch, now shows $1.996 per GPU-hour for its A100 SXM4 80 GB in one, two, four and eight-GPU sizes, up from the $1.79 we recorded at the end of September, with 22 CPUs and 120 GB of RAM listed against the card 19. Above that range, and only by the eight-GPU instance, Crusoe lists an A100 80 GB SXM at $2.30 per GPU-hour next to a PCIe version at $2.00, and Lambda sells its A100 SXM 80 GB as an eight-GPU instance at $2.79 per GPU with 240 vCPU, 1,800 GiB of RAM and 19.5 TiB of SSD 21 6.

results.title: B200 rental index hits record $8.54 per GPU-hour as CoreWeave slid: Orrn - Blockspace
results.author: William Foxley
highlights:
GPU data provider Ornn says its B200 GPU rental index hit a record of $8.54 per GPU-hour on Sunday, and its B300 index also set an all-time high, the compute exchange said Monday. Ornn said B200 rental prices rose 12.9% over the past trading week. Over the same week, shares of CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) fell 25.2%.

The B200 index eased 1.5% to $8.41 on Monday. It was still up 14.7% over seven days and 13.2% over 30 days. October’s average so far is $7.82, against $7.25 in September and $6.14 in August.

...

The index tracks only executed on-demand rentals, using a volume-weighted, winsorized mean over a rolling one-hour window. Reserved capacity, long-term agreements and forward contracts are excluded.
